previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with fever, sepsis, and multiple infected pressure ulcers on the sacral region and right hip, along with a traumatic ulcer on the left foot. He was started on IV daptomycin and meropenem for broad-spectrum coverage. The wound care and plastic surgery teams performed several bedside debridements. Although urine cultures grew E. coli and Klebsiella, the source of sepsis was attributed to the skin wounds. He developed transient hyperkalemia, which resolved with hydration. His nephrostomy stitch dislodged during admission and was secured with a stat lock. He completed a two-week antibiotic course and was discharged home with a new pressure-relief mattress, follow-up planned with plastic surgery, urology, nephrology, and infectious disease, and instructions to complete outpatient imaging for a known lung nodule.
